audience.programmeDescription: Hebrew Language and Culture at the University of Amsterdam combines modern and Biblical Hebrew with Jewish history, literature and intellectual traditions. The curriculum shown uses the university’s local alternative for students who cannot study abroad.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers comparative literature, philosophy, archaeology, and global history and politics. The available courses do not form a sequence in Jewish intellectual and cultural history, Hebrew textual traditions or Middle Eastern regional study. These subjects organise the University of Amsterdam’s degree and its research. The table shows the verified Amsterdam pathway.

componentNotes.heb-126121026y: This course starts in block 5, alongside Modern Hebrew Language Acquisition 4.
componentNotes.heb-126211416y: Requires Modern Hebrew Language Acquisition 4 or equivalent knowledge.
componentNotes.heb-126211426y: Requires the first 3000 jaar Hebreeuws course or equivalent knowledge.
componentNotes.heb-126221036y: Requires the second 3000 jaar Hebreeuws course or equivalent knowledge.
componentNotes.heb-126221116y: The first of five local courses that replace the 30-EC study-abroad semester for students who cannot travel.
componentNotes.heb-126221016y: Requires Biblical Hebrew or equivalent preparation.
componentNotes.heb-126219002y: Students are normally expected to complete the subject-specific courses before starting the thesis.
componentNotes.heb-approved-free-profiling-space: Choose 30 EC of eligible electives or a minor. An approved internship or study abroad may count.
